contexts.text: The dove found no rest for the sole of her foot () = that nothing of the good and truth of faith could yet take root.
To take by the palm () = to confide.

God hath seen the weariness of my palms () = that all things were from Himself by His Own power... The weariness of the palms = temptations... The palm, or hand, = power; consequently, my palms, or my hands = Own power.

He touched the hollow of his thigh () = where celestial spiritual good is conjoined with the natural good signified by Jacob... The hollow, or acetabulum, or the hollow of the thigh, = where there is conjunction.
The hollow of the thigh = where goods are conjoined.

He touched the hollow of Jacob's thigh = where conjugial love is conjoined with natural good; (for) the hollow of the thigh = where there is the conjunction of conjugial love. The reason why conjunction there with natural good is signified, is that there the thigh is conjoined with the feet...
This conjunction (of every celestial and spiritual love with natural good) is what is signified by the hollow of the thigh.
That the hollow of the thigh is where there is the conjunction of conjugial love with natural good, consequently where there is the influx of spiritual truth into natural good. References.
Hence to touch the hollow of the thigh, or to hurt it so as to occasion halting, = to destroy the good which is of those loves.
It became a rod in his palm () = that then power was communicated from the Divine... The palm = interior power.
The fists, or palms, = power, because the hand = power.
External or natural good was represented by, the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot (); for... the soles of the feet = the things which are ultimate, in the natural man. AE 279:2.

Thou shalt put all things upon the palms of Aaron, and upon the palms of his sons () = the acknowledgement in the Heavens that these things are the Lord's and from the Lord... (For) the palms = the things which are from Own power; thus proprium... The reason the palms = the things which are from Own power; and hence to be put upon the palms = the acknowledgement that all these things are the Lord's and from the Lord, is that the palms are those of the hands; and by the hands is signified power; and to put upon them = to ascribe; thus to acknowledge; for it follows that they were to be agitated upon them, by which is signified the derivative life from the Divine; and life from the Divine is given through faith, the first of which is acknowledgement. As by the hands is signified power, it follows that by the palms of the hands is signified full power, since the palms grasp fully; and therefore when the palms are predicated of the Lord, and of the Divine truth proceeding from His Divine good, as here, omnipotence is signified. Hence it is evident that to put upon the palms of Aaron and his sons = the acknowledgement of the Lord's omnipotence; thus that all things are His, because all things in the Heavens are from Him.

I will cover My palm upon thee, until I have passed by () = the closing up of the Internal... of the Church, of worship, and of the Word... for to cover with the palm involves to prevent from seeing the glory and faces of Jehovah...
And I will remove My palm, and thou shalt see My hinder parts... ()-that they should see the externals of the Word, of the Church, and of worship...
The sole of the steps of the king of Assyria () = the Sensuous and the derivative reasoning, which is from fallacies alone.
From the sole of the foot even to the head no soundness () = that both the natural and spiritual things... are destroyed.
